_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 8 Data and Information. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order (paper and digital databases; forms; data; information; raw data), in the lesson's own words. ONE COUNT RUNS THROUGH THE WHOLE FILM: the lesson's own eight children answer walk, bus, car, bike, walk, bus, walk, car - so walk 3, bus 2, car 2, bike 1, and 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 8. Every tally mark, every number and every spoken figure is that one count. Nothing here is a pictogram: one mark is one child.
title: Data and Information
subtitle: Grade 4 Computing
objectives: Understand the differences between physical (paper-based) and digital databases.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of using forms when collecting data.
Identify the differences between data and information.

beats.say: Walk, bus, car, walk. Four words, and no meaning at all.
Organise them, count them, and they tell you something. Data in, information out.
A database is an organised collection of data. It can live on paper, or on a computer.
On paper it is a box of cards, or a register of names.
On a computer it is the same data, stored digitally.
Digital is fast to search and to sort, easy to share, and very small.
Paper needs no power and no login, and cannot be reached from far away.
Digital is not better at everything. Each has its place.
A form asks everyone the same question, with the same choices.
How do you get to school? Walk, bike, car, or bus.

at.ask: How do you get to school?

beats.say: Amal walks. Sami takes the bus. Zara comes by car. Omar rides his bike.
Eight children answer, and every answer is written down the same way.
Everyone got the same question, so the answers can be counted. Nothing is missed.
But Hana comes by scooter, and scooter is not a choice.
A form cannot ask why, and a bad question gives wrong data from everyone.
Data is the raw facts: 21, walk, cat, size 2.
On its own, a fact like that means nothing at all.
Here are the eight answers again, exactly as the children gave them.

at.exactly: exactly as the children gave them

beats.say: Walk, bus, car, bike, walk, bus, walk, car. Which way do most children come?

at.list: Walk, bus, car, bike, walk, bus, walk, car
at.which: Which way do most children come?

beats.say: You cannot tell yet. A list of words is data, and nothing more.

at.listdata: A list of words is data

beats.say: Now organise it. Put every answer in a table, and count them.
Walk three. Bus two. Car two. Bike one. That is all eight children.
Now look at the counts. Most children walk to school.
Only one child cycles. That is information: what the data means.
Information is what you act on: a safe crossing, and one bike rack.
21, 19, 24, 22, 30. Five numbers, and no meaning at all.
That is raw data: facts as they were collected, before anybody used them.
Now say they are the temperatures in a classroom, at nine o'clock, on five days.
The last one was the day the heating stuck on. Now the numbers mean something.
Information is raw data that has been given a meaning.
A database is organised data, on paper or on a computer.
A form asks everyone the same question, and it cannot ask why.
Data is the raw facts. Information is what those facts mean.

at.information: Information is what those facts mean
